original_interpretation: WSTS Dec 2025 (Autumn 2025) forecast: 2026 market USD 975bn after est. USD 772bn in 2025.
evidence_found: "the global semiconductor market is now projected to grow 22 percent in 2025, reaching USD 772 billion"; "For 2026, WSTS forecasts the global semiconductor market to grow by more than 25 percent, reaching USD 975 billion." Table: Total World $M 772,243 / 975,460 (WSTS release, 2 Dec 2025, p.1-2)
correction: Accurate as a December 2025 forecast but superseded: WSTS Spring 2026 (2 Jun 2026) forecasts 2026 at USD 1,511,248m (+89.9%) (CLM-0032), and the final 2025 result was USD 795.6bn (+26.2%) (WSTS 6 Mar 2026, SRC-0862), not 772bn.
notes: Near-duplicate of CLM-0047/CLM-0048, which were also marked outdated. Growth stated in text as 22% (table 22.5%).

original_interpretation: US-HQ companies hold almost half the global SME market (SIA 2025).
evidence_found: "A 2024 SIA-Boston Consulting Group (BCG) report illustrated the degree of specialization... U.S.-headquartered companies lead in design and core IP, and command almost half the global market share in semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME)." (SIA SOTI 2025, p.20)
notes: SIA attributes the figure to the 2024 SIA/BCG report (data year likely 2022), so '(SIA, 2025)' is the citing document, not the data year. Share is by company headquarters (footnote 4).

original_interpretation: US-HQ companies: 50.4% of global semiconductor sales in 2024, USD 318bn.
evidence_found: "In 2024, the U.S. semiconductor industry continued that trend, with U.S. headquartered companies reaching sales of $318 billion, accounting for 50.4% of global sales revenue." (p.23); chart source "WSTS, Gartner, Omdia, and SIA Estimates"
notes: Duplicate of CLM-0076. Newer CY2025 figure (US$425bn, 53.4%) is in CLM-2305 (SIA 2026 report); this 2024 claim is still correct as dated.

original_interpretation: Computers/AI largest end use in 2024 at 34.9% of demand.
evidence_found: Chart "TOTAL GLOBAL DEMAND SHARE BY END USE, 2024" (p.24): PDF text layer row "Computers/AI" over "34.9% 9.9%" (Computers/AI left, Consumer Electronics right); text: "the computer market's share of chip sales increased by 10% from 2023 to become the largest segment in 2024"
notes: Label-value pairing checked against the PDF text layer coordinates and a visual reading. The researcher's note pairings were wrong: Communications is 33.0%, Automotive 12.7%, Consumer Electronics 9.9%, Industrial 8.4%, Government 1.0% (new claims in this batch). Newer: 2025 share 45.5% (CLM-1345).

original_interpretation: Automotive = 9.9% of global semiconductor demand in 2024.
evidence_found: Chart p.24, PDF text layer: label row "Automotive Government" (y=274) sits directly above value row "12.7% 1.0%" (y=255); "Computers/AI" and "Consumer Electronics" (y=398) sit above "34.9% 9.9%" (y=379). Visual reading confirms Automotive 12.7%, Consumer Electronics 9.9%.
correction: Automotive was 12.7% of 2024 demand; 9.9% is Consumer Electronics. New claim added (supersedes CLM-0561).
notes: The tool mis-mapped chart labels, as CLM-0073 warned. 12.7% fits SIA 2026's statement that automotive fell to 10.9% in 2025 (CLM-1346).

original_interpretation: Global SME sales USD 135.1bn in 2025, +15% from 117.1bn.
evidence_found: "Worldwide sales of semiconductor manufacturing equipment increased 15% to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $117.1 billion in 2024" (SEMI release, 7 Apr 2026, para 1)
notes: Duplicate of CLM-0057.

original_interpretation: China largest equipment market in 2025 at USD 49.3bn (~36%).
evidence_found: "In 2025, spending in China remained near record levels at $49.3 billion, down just 0.5% from the prior year"; Taiwan $31.5bn, Korea $25.8bn, North America $10.9bn, Japan $9.5bn, Europe $2.9bn, RoW $5.2bn (SEMI release, 7 Apr 2026)
notes: 49.3/135.1 = 36.5%; 'about 36%' is our arithmetic. China is the largest of the listed regions. Region = equipment ship-to location.

original_interpretation: Test equipment +55% in 2025 (AI/HBM), assembly & packaging +21%.
evidence_found: "Test equipment billings surged 55% year-over-year as AI devices and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) increased performance requirements and test intensity, while assembly and packaging equipment sales rose 21%" (SEMI release, 7 Apr 2026)

original_interpretation: Global semiconductor materials revenue USD 73.2bn in 2025, +6.8%.
evidence_found: "Global semiconductor materials market revenue increased 6.8% year-over-year to $73.2 billion in 2025" (SEMI release, 12 May 2026, para 1)

original_interpretation: 2025 wafer fab materials USD 45.8bn; packaging materials USD 27.4bn.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials revenue increased 5.4% to $45.8 billion." "Packaging materials revenue grew 9.3% to $27.4 billion in 2025." (SEMI release, 12 May 2026)

original_interpretation: Taiwan largest materials consumer for 16th year, USD 21.7bn in 2025.
evidence_found: "Taiwan remained the largest consumer of semiconductor materials for the 16th consecutive year, with revenue of $21.7 billion in 2025." (SEMI release, 12 May 2026)

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG: >50 points in the value chain where one region holds >65% share.
evidence_found: 2-pager: "There are more than 50 points across the value chain where one region holds more than 65% of the global market share." Full report p.5: "There are more than 50 points across the supply chain where one region holds more than 65% of the global market share"
notes: Dated 2021 estimate (data c. 2019); the full report adds 'although the level of risk associated with each of these varies'. Duplicate of CLM-0083.

original_interpretation: ~75% of global manufacturing capacity in China and East Asia (SIA/BCG 2021).
evidence_found: "About 75% of semiconductor manufacturing capacity, as well as many suppliers of key materials—such as silicon wafers, photoresist, and other specialty chemicals—are concentrated in China and East Asia" (full report p.5); 2-pager: "About 75% of global semiconductor manufacturing capacity...is concentrated in China and East Asia"
notes: Dated 2021 estimate (c. 2019 capacity). The 2024 SIA/BCG report has newer 2022/2032 capacity splits (SRC-0342/SRC-0863), which should be used for current shares. Duplicate of CLM-0117.

original_interpretation: All sub-10nm capacity in Taiwan (92%) and South Korea (8%) at the time of the 2021 study.
evidence_found: Full report p.5: "all of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity—in nodes below 10 nanometers—is currently located in South Korea (8%) and Taiwan (92%)." 2-pager: "100% of the world's most advanced (below 10 nanometers) semiconductor manufacturing capacity is currently located in Taiwan (92%) and South Korea (8%)."
notes: Source says 'semiconductor manufacturing capacity' below 10nm, not specifically logic (metric population says logic). Data year 2019 per USITC (see CLM-0116). Newer: 2024 SIA/BCG projects US <10nm share rising from ~0% (2022) to 28% (2032) (CLM-0549).

original_interpretation: Chip design = specification, logic design, physical design, validation and verification.
evidence_found: "Design involves specification, logic design, physical design, and validation and verification." (CSET, p.6)

original_interpretation: ATP: cut wafer into chips, mount on frame with wires, enclose in casing.
evidence_found: "Assembly, testing, and packaging starts with cutting a finished wafer—which contains dozens of chips in a grid pattern after fabrication (second image in Figure 2)—into separate chips. Each chip is mounted on a frame with wires that connect the chip to external devices, and enclosed in a protective casing." (p.7)

original_interpretation: Photolithography passes light through a photomask to transfer pattern to photoresist.
evidence_found: "A photolithography tool passes light through a “photomask”—a transparent plate with a circuit pattern—to transfer that pattern to the photoresist." (p.6)

original_interpretation: Core IP = reusable modular design portions; EDA = chip design software.
evidence_found: "EDA is software used to design chips." ... "Core IP consists of reusable modular portions of designs, allowing design firms to license and incorporate them in their designs." (p.6)

original_interpretation: EDA software market ~USD 6.8bn in 2019 (CSET).
evidence_found: Table 17 "2019 EDA and core IP market" (p.49): "EDA software $6.8 billion". Fn 189: "The $6.8 billion figure includes four segments in the EDA market: computer-aided engineering (CAE)...; design of printed circuit boards (PCB) and multi-chip modules (MCM); and chip physical design and verification...; and services."
notes: Caveat: CSET's figure includes PCB/MCM design and services, from ESD Alliance data (fn 189). Dated 2019. Near-duplicate of CLM-0415.

original_interpretation: US firms ~96% of EDA market in 2019; only full-spectrum leading-edge EDA providers.
evidence_found: Table 1 (p.8): "EDA 1.5% 96% <1% 3% 0% 0% <1% 0%" (value add, U.S., S. Korea, Japan, Taiwan, Europe, China, Other); fn 14: "Market shares are from 2019". p.50: "U.S. firms are the exclusive providers of EDA software with the full-spectrum capabilities needed by engineers at fabless firms and IDMs to design leading-edge chips."
notes: The quote is on printed p.50, not p.49. Shares are by firm headquarters (Mentor counted as U.S.).

original_interpretation: Core IP market ~USD 3.9bn in 2019; US ~52%, Europe ~43%.
evidence_found: Table 17 (p.49): "Core IP $3.9 billion ARM (U.K./Japan), Synopsys (U.S.), Cadence (U.S.)..."; Table 1 (p.8): "Core IP 0.9% 52% 0% 0% 1% 43% 2% 2%"; p.50: "U.S. and U.K. vendors dominate the market."
notes: Europe's 43% is largely Arm (UK-based, then SoftBank-owned). Dated 2019.

original_interpretation: CSET: Arm top core IP vendor; its ISA/IP underpins most smartphone processors.
evidence_found: "ARM is the top core IP vendor, providing an instruction set architecture (ISA) and associated core IP underpinning most of the world's smartphone processors." (p.51)
notes: Location is printed p.51, not p.50. The same passage refers to the Nvidia-Arm deal, which was later abandoned (not part of this claim).

original_interpretation: EUV scanner market ~USD 3.1bn in 2019, 100% ASML.
evidence_found: Table 9 "2019 lithography market" (p.30): "EUV scanners $3.1 billion ASML (Netherlands) None 0%"; p.32: "One Dutch firm, ASML, exclusively produces EUV scanners, the most advanced photolithography equipment."
notes: Table 9 lists ASML as the only firm and gives China 0%; it does not print '100%'. The 100% rests on the p.32 'exclusively produces' sentence.

original_interpretation: CSET lists five Japanese firms (JSR, TOK, Shin-Etsu, Fujifilm, Sumitomo) as photoresist producers.
evidence_found: Table 18 (p.56): "Photoresists $3.3 billion. JSR (Japan), Tokyo Ohka Kogyo (Japan), Shin-Etsu Chemical (Japan), Fujifilm Electronic Materials (Japan), Sumitomo Chemical (Japan), Dongjin (South Korea), DuPont Electronic Solutions (U.S.), EMD Performance Materials (U.S.), Inpria (U.S.), Ruihong (China)..."
correction: The five Japanese firms head CSET's list, but the same list also names Dongjin (South Korea), DuPont, EMD and Inpria (U.S.) and four Chinese firms. 'All Japanese' applies only to the five named firms, not to the producer list. Location is p.56.

original_interpretation: Top wafer producers HQ'd in Japan, Taiwan, Germany, South Korea; China minimal 300mm.
evidence_found: "Firms headquartered in Japan, Taiwan, Germany, and South Korea are top producers of wafers (Figure 29), especially 300 mm wafers, which China only minimally produces." (p.57)
notes: Location is p.57, not p.55. Dated 2021.

original_interpretation: Leading-edge photomasks led by Japan, US, Taiwan, South Korea (CSET 2021).
evidence_found: "Photomasks. Japan, the United States, Taiwan, and South Korea lead production of leading-edge photomasks (e.g., ≤16 nm), which China does not produce." (p.58)
notes: CSET defines leading-edge here as ≤16 nm. Location is p.58.

original_interpretation: TSMC held 54% of the world logic foundry market in CY2020 (CSET).
evidence_found: CSET p.22: "Market leader TSMC has 54 percent of the world's logic foundry market share" (fn 76 cites TrendForce, 19 Mar 2020). TrendForce table "Ranking of the Global Top 10 Foundries by Revenue, 1Q20": TSMC 1Q20E 10,200 (US$m), M/S 54.1%; Top 10 Total 18,060
correction: The 54% is TrendForce's March 2020 estimate for 1Q20 alone (54.1% of top-10 foundry revenue), not a full-year 2020 figure. A corrected claim is added (supersedes CLM-0552). Newer: TrendForce puts TSMC at 70.4% in 4Q25 (CLM-0068) and 72.5% in 2Q26 (CLM-0553).
notes: The metric period (CY2020) and population (all foundries) are wrong: the base is top-10 foundry revenue in one quarter, with Samsung including System LSI.

original_interpretation: OSAT market ~USD 28bn in 2019 (CSET).
evidence_found: Table 6 (p.24): "Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test $28 billion ASE (Taiwan), Amkor (U.S.), JCET (China)..."; fn 92: "OSAT market size is based on the top 25 OSAT vendors."; Appendix: "the 2019 OSAT market size ($28.2 billion)"
notes: Population is the top 25 OSATs' revenue, not the whole market. Dated 2019. Newer: DIGITIMES puts 2024 OSAT revenue at US$41.2bn (CLM-1026), a different method.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG value chain: pre-competitive research, design, front end, back end, plus an EDA/IP, equipment and materials ecosystem.
evidence_found: p.13: "At a high level, it consists of four broad steps, supported by a specialized ecosystem of materials, equipment and software design tools and core IP suppliers (Exhibit 4)"; Exhibit 4: "1. Pre-competitive research 2. Design 3. Front End Wafer fabrication 4. Back End Assembly, packaging & testing ... 6. Equipment & Tools 7. Materials"
notes: The p.13 sentence states the structure directly. Exhibit 4 counts 'seven differentiated activities' (EDA & core IP is the 5th).

original_interpretation: Fabrication and test use >50 types of specialised wafer processing/testing equipment.
evidence_found: "Semiconductor manufacturing uses more than 50 different types of sophisticated wafer processing and testing equipment provided by specialist vendors for each step in the fabrication process. (Exhibit 8)." (p.19)
notes: Exhibit 8 (p.20) shows '50+' equipment types and a $64B 2019 equipment market.

original_interpretation: Design ~65% of total industry R&D in 2019 (SIA/BCG).
evidence_found: p.15 text: "it accounts for 65% of the total industry R&D and 53% of the value added"; p.15 sidebar: "Chip design 53% of industry R&D"; p.22: "65% of the total industry R&D investment (excluding pre-competitive research) is made in the design layer"
correction: 65% excludes pre-competitive research (p.22). As a share of total industry R&D including pre-competitive research (15-20%), design is 53% (Exhibit 4 / sidebar). A corrected claim is added (supersedes CLM-0476).
notes: This resolves the researcher's note about Exhibit 4 showing 53%: both figures are right on different bases (53/82 = 65%).

original_interpretation: Design ~53% of industry value added in 2019 (SIA/BCG).
evidence_found: p.15 text: "it accounts for 65% of the total industry R&D and 53% of the value added"; p.15 sidebar: "Chip design 53% of industry R&D 13% of industry capex 50% of the value added"; Exhibit 4 value-add shares 50/24/6/4/11/5 (sum 100%)
correction: The text says 53%, but the same report's design sidebar and Exhibit 4 give 50% of value added, and those shares sum to 100%. Treat it as roughly 50-53%, with 50% the more consistent figure. A contradiction record is added.

original_interpretation: Wafer fabrication ~65% of industry capex in 2019 (SIA/BCG).
evidence_found: "As a result, wafer fabrication accounts for approximately 65% of the total industry capital expenditure and 25% of the value added." (p.18); sidebar p.16: "64% of industry capex 24% of the value added"
notes: Exhibit 4 gives 64%; 'approximately 65%' is consistent.

original_interpretation: Industry R&D ~USD 90bn globally in 2019 (SIA/BCG).
evidence_found: "Overall, we estimate that in 2019 the industry invested about $90 billion in R&D and $110 billion in capital expenditure globally across all the activities in the value chain." (p.22); Exhibit 4: "R&D $92B CAPEX $108B"
notes: Exhibit 4's $92B total includes pre-competitive research (15-20%). Dated 2019.
